title: HABIT 50+: Habitual toothbrushing behavior and intraoral scan–based plaque tracking in individuals aged 50 to 70
summary:
Background:
Good oral hygiene at home is important for preventing tooth decay and diseases of the gums and supporting tissues of the teeth. However, studies show that many people do not clean all areas of their teeth equally well. Toothbrushing is often unsystematic, and certain areas, especially the inner surfaces of the teeth, are brushed for too short a time or are not cleaned adequately.
Most previous studies have focused on children, adolescents and young adults. Comparatively little is known about the toothbrushing behaviour of people aged 50 to 70 years. This age group is particularly relevant because exposed root surfaces, gum recession, dental restorations and dental prostheses may promote plaque accumulation and increase the risk of tooth decay and diseases of the supporting tissues of the teeth.
It is also often unclear why certain areas are not cleaned sufficiently. Possible reasons include lack of motivation, unfavourable habits or difficulties with the practical and motor aspects of toothbrushing.
Plaque has traditionally been assessed using clinical plaque indices. However, these assessments partly depend on the judgement of the examiner. Intraoral scanners now make it possible to record plaque digitally and to assess its amount and distribution more objectively and reproducibly.

Aim of the study:
The aim of this study is to investigate the habitual toothbrushing behaviour of people aged 50 to 70 years. The study will assess how long and how systematically participants brush their teeth and which brushing movements they use.
In addition, the amount of plaque before and after toothbrushing will be measured, and areas that are cleaned well or less effectively will be identified. The study will then examine how the observed toothbrushing behaviour is related to plaque removal.

Study procedure:
After receiving written information about the study and after the eligibility criteria have been checked, participants will be asked to provide some information about their general and oral health.
Plaque will then be made visible using a disclosing agent and recorded with an intraoral scanner. Participants will subsequently be asked to brush their teeth in their usual way, using their own toothbrush and without a specified brushing time. The toothbrushing process will be video-recorded.
After toothbrushing, plaque will be disclosed again and a second intraoral scan will be obtained. The participant’s toothbrush and any other oral hygiene aids brought to the appointment will also be photographed. A short questionnaire will be used to assess, among other things, the perceived bristle stiffness and the participant’s usual brushing pressure.

Participants will then receive individual feedback and instructions on how to improve their oral hygiene. At their request, a professional tooth cleaning may subsequently be carried out; however, this is not part of the study.

Analysis:
The video recordings will be used to assess:
total and region-specific brushing duration,
the systematicity of toothbrushing,
the types of brushing movements used.

The intraoral scans will be used to determine:
the percentage of tooth surfaces covered by plaque before and after toothbrushing,
the distribution of plaque in different regions of the mouth,
the reduction in plaque achieved by toothbrushing.

interventions.name:
Video-based behavioural analysis:
Assessment of habitual toothbrushing behaviour, including brushing duration, systematicity, and brushing movements.

Intraoral scan-based plaque analysis:
Planimetric assessment of plaque coverage before and after toothbrushing and of the resulting plaque reduction.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Age 50–70 years (inclusive)
2)Informed consent and willingness to participate in the study
3) A maximum of one missing tooth per jaw (excluding third molars) that has not been replaced
Exclusion criteria:
1)Severe systemic or acute diseases (ASA > II)
2) Significant cognitive, motor, or neurological disorders (CFS > 3) Allergies or intolerances to the materials used in the study
4) Acute painful oral conditions
